own_solution.law: Conservation of mechanical energy gives v²/2 - GM/R = -GM/(R+h), with GM = g0 R². Thus h = v²R/(2g0R-v²). Using R = 1737000 m and v = 1500 m/s gives h = 1157.01268 km.
assumptions: The motor supplies the stated launch speed, after which the probe coasts under lunar gravity.
Any catapult speed supplied at the present firing adds to the motor's launch speed.
The earlier test does not alter the stated conditions of the present launch.
Lengths and speeds are converted to coherent units before numerical evaluation.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T9571 and T9D2A replace the numerical speed and its unit with 'a small amount', violating the required preservation of number and unit across variants of the same quantity.

notes: The physics, stratum assignments, cancellation relations and all certified numerical answers are correct. For either relevant sentence, additional speeds of 60, 210 and 330 m/s give heights of 1323.35, 1878.54 and 2552.47 km respectively. All resulting launch speeds are below the escape speed of approximately 2372.32 m/s. Probe mass cancels, and neither the relay capsule's speed nor the earlier test speed affects the present trajectory. The governing equations are dimensionally consistent; numerical evaluation requires converting the supplied radius from kilometres to metres and the resulting height back to kilometres. The explicitly named numerical minimal pairs preserve 210 m/s and change the intended object or event attachment. The authors identify the two numeral-free sentences as deliberate controls rather than numerical minimal pairs, but this does not satisfy the review instructions' requirement that variants of the same quantity preserve number and unit. I therefore retain the pass-1 defect. My pass-1 heights were expressed in metres; the pass-2 target is kilometres, so the numerical difference is solely a unit conversion.
